subject: Hosted API uplift — phased capacity bridge & billing cushion
messages:
From: Logan Wright <logan@redwood.com>
To: Elena Morales <elena@bluegrid.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 20 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Hosted API uplift — phased capacity bridge & billing cushion

Hi Elena —

Thanks again for the sync yesterday. Based on the ramp signals you shared and the Q2 usage extract, we sketched a low-friction pathway to get BlueGrid comfortable with a higher monthly commitment while protecting you from short-term billing shocks. Attached is a short phasing table and a sample billing cushion (credits + soft burst) you can share with procurement.

Proposed highlights: 
- Start with a 30% committed uplift for months 1–3 (guaranteed pool).
- Auto-burst band of 20% above commit for immediate seasonal spikes, billed at reduced burst rate.
- Month 4 onward: evaluate telemetry and move to a 60% committed lane if 3-week moving avg exceeds 50% of the initial uplift.
- Optional quarterly cadence for adjustments and an SLA-backed latency objective if you want dedicated priority routing.

Can you confirm whether BlueGrid procurement needs a formal SOW or if the DocuSign uplift amendment is sufficient? If you prefer, we can present the phasing table in a 30-minute ops call with your platform leads.

I’ll loop in Karthik for technical sizing and Naomi for billing mechanics.

Thanks,
Logan Wright
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
loganw@redwood.com
+1 (650) 555-0142

Attachments: proposed-phasing-table.xlsx (xlsx) — outline of commit bands and sample billing cushion

Logan —

This looks reasonable and much easier to justify than jumping straight to a 6-month big commit. Procurement wants an amendment they can sign (prefer DocuSign), and Samir from platform wants the burst behavior documented (how we fail to fallback if we hit sustained overload). Two quick asks: 
1) Can you add a short note on prefix caching and how that affects effective token consumption for our high-variance endpoints?
2) We need a sample invoice illustration showing how the cushion credits apply when we go over the committed band.

If you can send a version with those two sections, procurement will likely approve this week.

— Elena

Adding the technical clarifications Elena asked for. Short version: 

- Prefix/KV caching: endpoints with repeated prompt prefixes (search + context) will see ~18–35% fewer generated tokens depending on cache hit rates; we’ll include a conservative 20% uplift reduction in the sample invoice to avoid surprises.
- Burst behavior: bursts are handled by the soft-band router. Short spikes under the burst band are served at the burst rate; sustained load beyond the burst band triggers a configurable backpressure policy — either queue with degraded latency (default) or fail-fast with 503s if the customer elects hard-fail. For BlueGrid I recommend queue-with-degraded-latency for the first 90 days.

I attached a compact ops note that can be included in the amendment (ops note attached to this message).

Karthik
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference

Attachments: bluegrid_usage_report_q2.csv (csv) — sample usage slice; ops-brief-soft-burst.txt (txt)

Thanks for the prompt review. Attached is a one-page invoice example that shows: committed monthly charge, burst usage calculation (burst units at reduced rate), and the credit cushion applied in month-of-invoice. We’ve assumed a 20% conservative reduction for caching as Karthik suggested; we can remove that line-item if you prefer raw usage.

Next steps we propose:
- You sign the uplift amendment via DocuSign (link below).
- We turn on the burst cushion immediately after DocuSign completes; billing will reflect the cushion on the following invoice cycle.
- Ops kickoff: 30-minute call (preferred) to configure backpressure policy and monitoring dashboard (we’ll invite Karthik + our support lead).
